issues.claim: Even this safety net is not guaranteed: on .NET 10, as on every .NET Core-based version, finalizers are not run when the process exits.
issues.problem: The fetched Object.Finalize excerpt does not support this claim. Its shutdown text reads "The runtime continues to finalize objects during shutdown only while the number of finalizable objects continues to decrease". That is the .NET Framework wording and, read on its own, suggests finalizers do run at shutdown. The cut-off excerpt shows no .NET Core note. The claim is true as far as I know, but the rebuttal only points to sibling questions citing the same page, which is not evidence from the item. A learner could be confused by the cited page.
issues.suggestedFix: Either drop the sentence and say only that the finalizer is not guaranteed to run (the Object.Finalize page lists cases where it does not run at all). Or cite the C# finalizers page, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/programming-guide/classes-and-structs/finalizers, which states that finalizers are not run at process exit in .NET Core and .NET 5+, and add it to links and linkTitles in both locales.
